title: The DOM
canDo: select and change page elements with JavaScript

blocks.md: Your HTML file is a blueprint. Once the browser reads it, it builds a **live object tree** in memory called the DOM — and JavaScript can reach into that tree to read, change, add, or remove anything on the page, right now, without a reload. That's the entire magic trick behind every interactive website you've ever used.

blocks.canDo: select and change page elements with JavaScript
blocks.md: By the end of this session you will be able to **select and change page elements with JavaScript** — grabbing nodes with `querySelector`, updating text with `textContent`, toggling styles with `classList`, and creating or removing elements on the fly.

The **Document Object Model** is the browser's in-memory representation of your HTML as a tree of *nodes*. Every tag becomes an element node; every piece of text becomes a text node. `document` is the root.

A handful of operations cover almost every real-world task:

- **Select** — `document.querySelector('#id')` returns the first matching element; `querySelectorAll` returns a list.
- **Read/write text** — `element.textContent` gets or sets the element's plain text.
- **Toggle classes** — `element.classList.add/remove/toggle('class')` lets CSS do the visual work.
- **Create/remove** — `document.createElement('tag')`, `parent.append(child)`, `element.remove()`.
- **Set properties** — assign element properties directly to control behaviour beyond styling, e.g. `button.disabled = true` to disable a button or `input.value = ''` to clear a field.

The DOM is *live*: the moment you change it, the browser repaints.

blocks.md: **`innerHTML` vs `textContent`** — `textContent` only sets plain text and is safe from injection attacks. Reserve `innerHTML` for when you genuinely need to insert HTML markup, and always sanitize user-supplied strings before using it.

questions.question: Which method returns the *first* element that matches a CSS selector?
questions.explanation: querySelector returns the first matching element; querySelectorAll returns a NodeList of all matches.

questions.question: You have a button element stored in `btn`. Which line *toggles* the CSS class `active` on it?
questions.explanation: classList.toggle adds the class if absent and removes it if present — one method for both states.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence to create a new `<li>` and add it inside an existing `<ul id="list">`?
questions.explanation: createElement creates the node; append inserts it as the last child of the target parent.

blocks.md:
You now know how to navigate the DOM tree, select elements with `querySelector`, update text via `textContent`, toggle classes with `classList`, and build or remove nodes programmatically. These four tools unlock virtually all static-page interactivity.

Next up: **Events** — making the page respond to what the user actually does.
